notes:
Summary: evaluation for Dedicated capacity with strict latency SLO alignment. Primary intent is migrating customer-facing support agent + reranking layer to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and throughput, with fallbacks to hosted variants.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-14: Intro call (Sofia, Daniel, CTO Maria Alvarez). Customer: wants hard p95/p99 commitments for non-streaming ops.
- 2026-02-21: Architecture deep-dive; validated network topology (VPC peering), KMS integration notes, initial capacity targets recorded.
- 2026-02-28: Security questionnaire submitted; SSO/SAML and SOC2 required.
- 2026-03-03: POC kickoff — synthetic traffic generator handed off. Planned 72h stress run.
- 2026-03-09: Pre-test checkpoint; adjusted batch sizing & KV cache strategy.
- 2026-03-11: On-site performance workshop scheduled (remote).

Use-case & SLO details (customer language & asks):
- Primary workloads: conversational support agent (approx 65% of requests streaming), embedding/reranking for search (25%), async summarization (10%).
- Throughput target: steady-state 1200 requests/sec during peak 4-hour window, burst to 2000 rps for 5–10m spikes.
- Latency SLOs requested: non-streaming generation p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 420ms (end-to-end, client-observed). For streaming responses: want first-chunk client RTT p50 <= 60ms, subsequent-chunk p95 <= 120ms, 99th chunk latency tracked separately.
- Customer explicitly wants clarification on what "end-to-end" means: client-side timing (includes mobile network) vs server-side service time. They want Redwood to define measurement attribution in SLA.

Measurement alignment notes (discussion points we need to close):
- Redwood server-side measurement: model inference time + queueing + egress to Redwood edge. Does NOT include last-mile mobile network. Customer insists on a mixed metric: server-side p99 + client-observed tail percentiles for a representative cohort.
- Proposed compromise: Redwood SLOs defined on server-side p50/p95/p99 over 30-day rolling windows; customer will accept credits if server-side p99 exceeds threshold AND their client-side telemetry (sampled SDK metrics) corroborates increased tail.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: treat first-byte latency separately. For streaming, measure first-chunk latency p50/p95 and per-chunk inter-arrival p95 to ensure smooth UX.
- Aggregation & windows: agreed to 30-day rolling window for SLA ops with daily health checks; penalties only if sustained breach over 3 consecutive days or a single 24h severe outage.
- Measurement sources: Redwood edge logs + sampled client SDK traces. Need to finalize a shared instrumentation spec (trace ids, time sync, sampling rate).

POC & testing plan (technical):
- Synthetic load generator will emulate 65% streaming conversations using chunk sizes and token rates matching production traces.
- E2E test will include: server-side telemetry, sampled client SDK traces (10k users), and on-prem network emulation (100–200ms mobile variance).
- Key metrics to collect: server_infer_ms, queue_ms, egress_ms, first_chunk_ms, chunk_interval_ms, token_throughput_tps, GPU_utilization_per_slot, batching_efficiency.
- Reserved GPU planning: preliminary sizing = 8 x A100-equivalent slots for baseline 1.2k rps with target avg token latency; propose burst pool of 2 nodes with autoscale guardrails.

SLA negotiation items outstanding:
- Exact definition of "server-side p99" (include queueing or not).
- Measurement authority: Redwood telemetry vs joint-run dashboards (Grafana read-only for customer).
- Credit formula: sliding scale tied to duration & severity. Customer asked for faster credit processing (30 days).

Quotes / paraphrases from PO: "If the p99 blips, our CX costs spike — we need deterministic tail behaviour, not averages."

Open action items (owner):
- SE (Daniel): finalize instrumentation spec + sample SDK patch (due 2026-03-14).
- AE (Sofia): draft SLA language w/ proposed SLO definitions and credit table (due 2026-03-18).
- Security (Amina): schedule penetration test and confirm KMS flow (due 2026-03-22).
- Engineering: run 72h synthetic E2E test and deliver results + raw logs to customer (start 2026-03-20).

Next steps (short):
- Align on "end-to-end" definition in SLA (this week).
- Run agreed E2E stress test with streaming/non-streaming mix.
- Post-test review meeting to lock sizing + pricing.

Procurement notes: customer prefers 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly usage true-up. They asked for an explicit break-out of committed vs burst pricing and a clause for model-variant fallback (downgrade to quantized variant) with defined latency/cost tradeoffs.
